messages:
raj: Hey team — we just had an incident after an automatic region failover. Traffic from EU customers got routed to eu-1 and responses suddenly changed format and token counts doubled. Billing spiked for one tenant. Request id: req_0a9f2c. Sample curl: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-base-v1\",\"input\":\"Summarize: AI safety\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate`. Response contained `model_served: compat-legacy-lite` and tokens=482 for a short prompt.
liv: Thanks @raj — sorry about that. Can you paste the raw response body and the route headers (x-redwood-region, x-redwood-variant, x-request-id)?
raj: Pasted below. headers: x-redwood-region: eu-1, x-redwood-variant: compat-legacy-lite, x-request-id: req_0a9f2c. Body: `{\"id\":\"req_0a9f2c\",\"model\":\"compat-legacy-lite\",\"tokens\":482,\"output\":\"...weird tokenized split\"}`. Expected redwood-base-v1 (same model they requested) — variant mismatch looks silent.
support-bot: :rotating_light: Incident created: #INC-4628. Assigned to support oncall.
liv: This looks like our region fallback policy selected a lighter legacy variant when eu-1 GPU pool was constrained. Two issues: 1) variant is not tokenizer-compatible with redwood-base-v1 (vocab/encoding differs) 2) token accounting is higher -> billing delta. I'll escalate to eng-runtime.
marco: @liv seeing logs for req_0a9f2c now. Runtime fallback decision: capacity_rule -> prefer_low_latency then fallback_to_compatible where compat matrix erroneously included compat-legacy-lite as compatible. That variant uses a different tokenizer (bpe_v2 vs bpe_v1). We need to fix the compatibility matrix and surface warnings.
sienna: Can you confirm whether the fallback was triggered due to memory OOM or preflight capacity check? I see eu-1 had a transient spike at 2025-03-12T09:44:55Z.
marco: Trigger was `capacity_shortfall` on model redwood-base-v1 at 09:44:53Z. Fallback policy executed because `allow_variant_fallback=true` for this customer. The bad part: no `tokenizer_compatibility_check` was run before swap.
raj: Customer observed garbled stop sequences and some hallucinated tokens. They also reported a 403 on a subsequent request (we think due to signed token mismatch?).
liv: The 403 could be from signature check when we rerouted to eu-1 ephemeral gateway that had stale HMAC key. Need infra to confirm key sync.
sienna: Key sync logs show a 90s rotation lag at that time — gateway accepted requests but returned 403 for certain signed headers. Investigating.
marco: Immediate mitigation steps: 1) set `allow_variant_fallback=false` on the customer's routing policy (temporary) 2) add an explicit preflight `tokenizer_check=true` in runtime so we don't swap to incompatible variant 3) roll forward a fix to the compatibility matrix (PR incoming).
liv: Raj — can you run this repro and send the `x-original-model` and `x-served-variant` headers? Also include the raw tokens array if possible. Quick curl to pin region: `curl -H \"x-redwood-region: us-west-2\" -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" ...`.
raj: Re-ran with region pin to us-west-2 — response now correct, model redwood-base-v1 served, tokens=67. Attached the raw tokens: `[101, 2054, 102]` (shortened). When routed to eu-1 earlier tokens looked like `[2,14,4096,...]` and splits mid-word.
marco: Good repro. I'm creating runtime task for a rule change: disallow fallback across tokenizer families and add a hard check that compares vocabulary fingerprint before swap. Also will emit a `model_mismatch_warning` event to the request path so we can alert support earlier.
bill-ops: For billing impact — capture all requests with `x-request-id` in window 09:40-09:50Z and mark for review; we can issue credit for unusual spikes caused by variant mismatch. Please add request ids to INC-4628.
liv: Assigning to eng-runtime (marco) and infra (sienna) for follow-up. Raj — I'll coordinate customer communication. Proposed message: apologise, explain failover to legacy variant due to capacity, confirm we've disabled automatic fallback for them, and offer to credit excess usage while we fix.
raj: That's perfect. One more ask from the customer: can we provide a reproducible test script that asserts tokenizer compatibility so they can detect this client-side? Might help.
marco: I'll add a tiny endpoint `/v1/test-tokenizer` that returns vocabulary fingerprint for a model and a sample tokenization. For now share this quick check: `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{\"model\":\"redwood-base-v1\",\"input\":\"testing tokenizer\"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/tokenize` — compare outputs across regions.
liv: Thanks everyone. I'll update INC-4628 with mitigation steps and ETA for PR. :white_check_mark:
